How to test on your iPhone

TWO RUNS
  1. 01

    Choose this iPhone’s speaker.

    Disconnect headphones and Bluetooth audio. Set a comfortable volume and keep it fixed for both runs. Start with Sound on and 4K preferred.

  2. 02

    Frame a bright, still scene.

    Enable camera only. Use crisp edges or texture, such as printed text, a shelf, or a patterned ceiling. Daylight works well; avoid filming a light bulb or blank wall. Rest the phone securely with its rear camera unobstructed. Do not hold it. A phone laid screen-down can point its rear camera toward the ceiling.

  3. 03

    Start, then hands off.

    Tap Start. A 5-second countdown gives you time to set the phone down. Recording then runs for 80 seconds, with automatic tones after 10 seconds. Keep this page in the foreground and the screen awake.

  4. 04

    Save video and settings.

    The video has no audio track. Use Share or Save for both files. Preserve the original video file, without messaging-app compression.

  5. 05

    Repeat with Muted control.

    Tap New recording, choose Muted control, and enable the camera again. Repeat with the same quality, position, scene, light, and system volume. The app silences the tone output for you. Save both files again.

What this experiment can tell us +

This is a recording pilot inspired by camera acoustic-sensitivity research. It does not implement Side Eye’s signal extraction or classifier. A flat-looking preview cannot rule out tiny image changes. Exported videos are compared with the known tone schedule and muted control before attempting words.

The browser requests a rear-facing camera, 4K or 1080p, and up to 60 fps. Delivered settings can differ. The camera label is shown where available; Safari may select a different rear lens. * Preview delivery measures displayed frame callbacks, not the sensor’s row timing or guaranteed encoded-video frame rate. No claims about rolling-shutter frequency are made.

Where exposed, focus and exposure are requested in manual mode with current values, and electronic stabilization is requested off. Safari may hide or reject those controls. Browser APIs cannot guarantee that optical stabilization is off. The report records capabilities, attempted controls, actual settings, callback timing, tone timing, and any interruption. Video is compressed; the bitrate is requested, not guaranteed.

No microphone track is requested, mixed, or recorded. Tone playback is output only. No speech recognition API, server upload, or analytics is used. Videos and reports remain local until you share or download them. If you leave the tab, the camera ends, or the file limit is reached, the partial video is retained while this page stays open.

Keep both original videos and both JSON reports. A native recorder may be needed if browser camera controls or compression obscure the effect. Speech recovery on your iPhone remains unproven.

Research: Side Eye, IEEE Security & Privacy 2023 ↗
